# Alert Dialog

> A modal dialog that asks before something can't be undone. Focus starts on Cancel, and a click outside doesn't close it.

`<slab-alert-dialog>` · Overlays · built on `<dialog role=alertdialog>`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/alert-dialog/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/alert-dialog.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-alert-dialog
  label="Delete this file?"
  description="It can't be recovered."
>
  <form method="dialog">
    <button value="delete">Delete</button>
  </form>
</slab-alert-dialog>
```

It's [Dialog](dialog.md) for a question that needs an answer, such as
confirming a delete. Screenreaders announce it as an alert dialog and read its
description along with its label as it opens.

Its Cancel button is built in, and focus starts there, so Enter pressed out of
habit doesn't do the thing it's asking about. Put the action that does it in the
default slot, usually a `<form method="dialog">` button: when it closes,
`returnValue` is that button's `value`, or empty when it was canceled. Slot an
`[autofocus]` element in instead when the dialog asks for something typed.

A click outside doesn't close it, so `closedby="any"` is treated as
"closerequest".

## Keyboard

| Key            | What it does                                                                                              |
| -------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Tab, Shift+Tab | Moves focus between Cancel and the dialog's other controls. The rest of the page is inert.                |
| Escape         | Closes the dialog, as Cancel does, unless `closedby` is "none". "cancel" can be canceled to keep it open. |
| Enter, Space   | On Cancel, closes the dialog with an empty `returnValue`.                                                 |

## Elements

### `<slab-alert-dialog>`

Import `slab-elements/alert-dialog.js` to register it.

A dialog with no visual styles that asks for a decision before anything else can happen: "Delete this file?". It's Dialog, with a `[role=alertdialog]` on its `<dialog>`, so screenreaders announce it as urgent, and the description is read along with the label as it opens.

It always has a Cancel button, built in, and that's where focus goes when it opens. The APG puts initial focus on the least destructive control, so Enter pressed out of habit doesn't delete anything. An `[autofocus]` element in it wins over the Cancel button, for a dialog that asks for something typed. Cancel closes it with an empty `returnValue`. Slot the action that does what the dialog asks into the default slot, usually as a `<form method="dialog">` button, so its `value` becomes `returnValue` as it does with Dialog.

There's no light dismiss. A click outside it does nothing, because an alert dialog wants an answer. `closedby="any"` is treated as "closerequest". Escape still closes it, as Cancel does, and dispatches "cancel", which can be canceled to keep it open. Set `closedby="none"` to turn Escape off where the browser supports it.

Everything else is Dialog's: `open`, `returnValue`, `close(returnValue)`, the label, and "cancel" and "close" from the host.

#### Attributes

| Name           | Type                                | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cancel-label` | `string`                            |         | The Cancel button's text and so its accessible name. "Cancel" in English when unset.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `closedby`     | `'any' \| 'closerequest' \| 'none'` |         | Passed to the `<dialog>`. "none" keeps Escape from closing it where the browser supports that. "any" is treated as "closerequest", since an alert dialog doesn't close on a click outside it.                                                                                                   |
| `description`  | `string`                            |         | What the dialog is asking, read with the label when it opens. Plain text. Slot into "description" for more.                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `hide-label`   | `boolean`                           | `false` | Hides the label visually and leaves it as the accessible name, for a design that shows the label some other way.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `label`        | `string`                            |         | Names it. It's the accessible name, and the visible label where there is one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `modal`        | `boolean`                           | `false` | Opens it as a modal when `open` is set, as `showModal()` does, for a modal opened declaratively. Not on a native `<dialog>`, where `open` always opens a non-modal one. `show()` and `showModal()` open it as they say whatever it is, and a change while it's open waits for it to open again. |
| `open`         | `boolean`                           | `false` | Whether it's open. Setting it opens it non-modally, as `open` does on a `<dialog>`, unless `modal` is set.                                                                                                                                                                                      |

#### Properties

| Name          | Type     | Description                                                                                               |
| ------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `returnValue` | `string` | The `<dialog>`'s, so `close(returnValue)` and a `<form method="dialog">` set it the way they do natively. |

#### Methods

| Signature                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `close(returnValue?: string): void`        | Closes it, setting `returnValue` to the value given, as a native dialog's `close()` does.                                                                           |
| `requestClose(returnValue?: string): void` | Asks it to close, as a native dialog's `requestClose()` does: "cancel" first, then a close that sets `returnValue` to the value given, unless "cancel" is canceled. |
| `show(): void`                             | Opens it non-modally, as a native dialog's `show()` does, whether or not `modal` is set. The rest of the page stays interactive.                                    |
| `showModal(): void`                        | Opens it as a modal, as a native dialog's `showModal()` does, whether or not `modal` is set.                                                                        |

#### Events

| Name     | Type          | Description                                                                                                                                           |
| -------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cancel` | `Event`       | When something asks it to close: Escape, a click outside with `closedby="any"`, or `requestClose()`. Cancel it to keep it open, as a native dialog's. |
| `toggle` | `ToggleEvent` | When it opens or closes, as a `ToggleEvent` with `oldState` and `newState` that doesn't bubble, as a popover's does.                                  |
| `close`  | `Event`       | When it closes, as a native dialog's does.                                                                                                            |

#### Slots

| Name          | Type                | Description                                                                                                 |
| ------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `description` | `Element \| string` | Text that describes it, such as a hint or what the validity message means. It's its accessible description. |
| (default)     | `Element \| string` | The action that does what the dialog asks, such as a Delete button in a form with method="dialog".          |
| `label`       | `Element \| string` | Its heading, in place of `label`                                                                            |

#### CSS parts

| Name          | Description                                                    |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cancel`      | The Cancel button. Closes the dialog with an empty returnValue |
| `description` | The description                                                |
| `dialog`      | The native dialog. A modal one's backdrop is its ::backdrop    |
| `label`       | The label                                                      |

#### CSS states

| Name           | Description      |
| -------------- | ---------------- |
| `:state(open)` | While it's open. |
